papers.title: Goal-Oriented Medium Access with Distributed Belief Processing
papers.abstract: Goal-oriented communication entails the timely transmission of updates related to a specific goal defined by the application. In a distributed setup with multiple sensors, each individual sensor knows its own observation and can determine its freshness, as measured by Age of Incorrect Information (AoII). This local knowledge is suited for distributed medium access, where the transmission strategies have to deal with collisions. We present Dynamic Epistemic Logic for Tracking Anomalies (DELTA), a medium access protocol that limits collisions and minimizes AoII in anomaly reporting over dense networks. Each sensor knows its own AoII, while it can compute the belief about the AoII for all other sensors, based on their Age of Information (AoI), which is inferred from the acknowledgments. This results in a goal-oriented approach based on dynamic epistemic logic emerging from public information. We analyze the resulting DELTA protocol both from a theoretical standpoint and with Monte Carlo simulations, showing that it is significantly more efficient and robust than classical random access, while outperforming state-of-the-art scheduled schemes by at least 30%, even with imperfect feedback.

papers.title: Resilient Collaborative Caching for Multi-Edge Systems With Robust Federated Deep Learning
papers.abstract: Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) leverages edge servers to provide computational power and storage resources for mobile users, but edge servers are heterogeneous and have limited storage. Recently, the deep learning (DL) model has been widely utilized to predict users' future content requests for proactive caching. However, the centralized training manner of DL models in existing caching schemes seriously suffers the risks of data privacy and significant communication overhead. Federated learning (FL) offers a promising approach to train DL models for collaborative caching in a distributed manner, thus protecting user privacy. Nevertheless, existing FL-based caching schemes focus only on the improvement of cache hit ratio and neglect the resource consumption of federated caching. Moreover, they fail to achieve robust caching when edge servers drop out of the FL process. To fill this gap, we propose a resilient FL-based collaborative caching scheme (RFL-Cache) to simultaneously maximize the cache hit ratio, minimize energy consumption and tolerate edge server dropouts in MEC systems. Specifically, we first formulate the caching problem as a multi-objective optimization problem. Then, we design a resilient FL-based collaborative caching algorithm for optimizing cache hit ratio and energy consumption, which successfully aggregates the contributions of edge servers even if some edge servers drop out. Moreover, we utilize the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) to train the DL model for RFL-Cache in a distributed manner. Extensive simulation results demonstrate that RFL-Cache outperforms various baselines in cache hit ratio by up to 31.7% and reduces energy consumption by up to 41.2% in the dropout case, while guaranteeing the convergence of the learning process in multi-edge systems.
